mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last two weeks (-32.7 to -23.6), indicating an activity rebound that should persist as pent-up demand continues to be released, pushing the next-28-day mean higher than the last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -32.7 to -23.6 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: If the next 28-day mean RETAIL_REC is equal to or lower than the last 28-day mean despite the two-week improving trend, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week jump in PARKS (-11.1 to -3.7) signals loosening of outdoor mobility restrictions; once PARKS crosses above -5, nearby retail and recreation venues see a corresponding increase in footfall within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -11.1 to -3.7 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks after PARKS crosses above -5, or falls instead, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES (-15.7 to -21.7) combined with persistently depressed TRANSIT (around -32) jointly indicate renewed mobility restrictions being enforced, which will suppress discretionary retail trips over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week while TRANSIT stays below -30
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped from -15.7 to -21.7 while TRANSIT remained near -32
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next four weeks despite the joint WORKPLACES drop and low TRANSIT, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has stayed persistently elevated (19.7-21.0) across all four weeks, reflecting a stable behavioral preference for staying home that will cap any retail rebound as long as this regime of high residential dwelling persists.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed in a narrow 19.7-21.0 band across four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises substantially over the next two weeks while RESIDENTIAL remains flat or elevated, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The t-0w jump in RETAIL_REC (-32.7 to -23.6) coincides with a short-term seasonal or holiday effect (e.g., a public holiday week) rather than a structural trend, so the uplift will partially reverse within one week once the seasonal effect passes.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC weekly jump exceeds 8 points in a single week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC jumped 9.1 points in the latest week, the largest single-week move in the snapshot
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to rise or holds its gain in the week immediately following the spike rather than partially reverting, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Low TRANSIT usage (~-32) combined with high RESIDENTIAL (~20) over four weeks indicates sustained behavioral caution about commuting and public spaces; this caution will lag any retail rebound signal and dampen RETAIL_REC growth over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT remained near -32 to -35 and RESIDENTIAL near 20 across all four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises consistently over the next four weeks despite TRANSIT and RESIDENTIAL remaining at current depressed/elevated levels, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The reversal in WORKPLACES from improving (-23.0 to -15.7) to declining (-15.7 to -21.7) suggests a policy tightening event; such reversals historically precede renewed restrictions that pull RETAIL_REC down within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES reverses direction and falls more than 5 points after two weeks of improvement
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved for two weeks then fell from -15.7 to -21.7
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the following two weeks despite the WORKPLACES reversal, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained stable and slightly positive (3.0 to 5.3) across all four weeks, indicating essential-trip activity is saturated and stable; this stability implies no additional essential-trip substitution effect will further boost or suppress RETAIL_REC, so RETAIL_REC movement will be driven by other factors and is expected to hold near its recent elevated level in the short term.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within a narrow 3.0-5.3 band across four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC drops sharply in the next week while GROCERY_PHARM remains flat, the hypothesis is rejected.
